identity.title: VALUEFLOW: Toward Pluralistic and Steerable Value-based Alignment in Large Language Models

problem.claim: Aligning LLMs with diverse human values while capturing deeper motivational principles.

gap.claim: Existing value-based approaches are described as lacking hierarchical extraction, calibrated intensity evaluation, and sufficient understanding of controlled-intensity steerability.

contributions.claim: Introduces VALUEFLOW, a unified framework for value extraction, evaluation, and steering with calibrated intensity control.
Combines HiVES for hierarchical value structure, VIDB for intensity-labeled texts, and an anchor-based evaluator for intensity scoring against VIDB panels.
Reports a large-scale study spanning ten models and four value theories, examining steerability asymmetries and composition laws for multi-value control.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present VALUEFLOW as unified infrastructure spanning extraction, evaluation, and steering of value intensity, including hierarchical embeddings, an intensity resource, and anchor-based evaluation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report findings on asymmetries in steerability and composition laws for multi-value control across ten models and four value theories.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diverse human values and deeper motivational principles remain difficult to capture with preference-based alignment.
The abstract identifies missing hierarchical extraction, calibrated intensity evaluation, and controlled-intensity steerability understanding.
VALUEFLOW unifies extraction, evaluation, and steering through HiVES, VIDB, and an anchor-based evaluator.
The authors study ten models and four value theories, reporting steerability asymmetries and multi-value composition laws.
The paper describes the framework as scalable infrastructure for evaluating and controlling value intensity in pluralistic alignment.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns each identified limitation with a corresponding framework capability: hierarchical structure with HiVES, intensity data with VIDB, and calibrated output scoring with an anchor-based evaluator.

lessons.interpretation: A limitation-to-component mapping makes the proposed design rationale easy to inspect.
lessons.application: When presenting a multi-part method, explicitly pair each stated gap with the component intended to address it.
lessons.exception: This mapping is unsuitable when components serve overlapping purposes or when the abstract cannot establish the claimed correspondence.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, evaluation metrics, model identities, value-theory identities, or details of the reported composition laws.
It does not specify how intensity calibration or steerability asymmetries were measured.
